title: The English Opening
description: A flexible flank opening starting with 1.c4. White fights for the center from the side and can transpose into many structures, keeping the opponent guessing.

sections.title: Controlling d5
sections.content: 1.c4 stakes a claim on the d5 square without committing the center pawns. White keeps options open and often fianchettoes the king's bishop for long-diagonal pressure.

positions.commentary: The English Opening. White controls d5 from the wing and retains maximum flexibility about the central structure.

sections.title: The Reversed Sicilian
sections.content: If Black answers 1...e5, the position resembles a Sicilian Defense with colors reversed — and an extra tempo for White. Understanding Sicilian themes helps here.

positions.commentary: A Reversed Sicilian. White enjoys Sicilian-style play with an extra move, often fianchettoing to pressure the long diagonal.
hints: Aim the bishop at the center

exercises.title: Develop Naturally
exercises.description: Black to play. Develop a knight toward the center to support e5.
